subject: Borealis: elevated 5xx/429 + retry spiral — status & exec coordination
messages:
From: Tom Jensen <tom.jensen@borealis.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: customer-sre@borealis.ai, ops@borealis.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] Traffic spike -> 5xx/429s + client retry amplification

Soojin —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your API around 07:50 PDT. Our SDK clients have been retrying aggressively and we’re observing a retry spiral that’s pushed request rates to ~3-4x baseline and caused user-facing timeouts.

Impact: several production campaigns failing, latency > 10s for some requests, and customers are opening tickets. We’ve attached a short set of log snippets showing the 429/5xx mix.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether this is capacity-related or a software regression?
- ETA on mitigation and whether you’ll post a public status update.
- Any temp mitigation (rate-limits, disable retries) you can apply that won’t break clients.

We need an initial status in the next 15 minutes. I’m looping in our SRE and will relay updates to internal stakeholders.

— Tom Jensen
VP Product, Borealis AI
ops@borealis.ai

- Rishi: collect quick kernel/runtime traces + tail the front-door LB metrics; look for error class (model OOM, runtime 5xx, client aborts).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Jensen <tom.jensen@borealis.ai>, customer-sre@borealis.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Traffic spike -> 5xx/429s + client retry amplification

On it — quick findings from infra:
- Dedicated GPU pool for Borealis is at 92% utilization across requests; queue depth has spiked. No recent deploys within the last 6 hours.
- Front door (ingress controller) logs show a pattern of 429s from our rate-limiter when concurrent connections spike. There are also sustained 500 traces from the runtime indicating transient KV cache misses being retried heavily.

Immediate mitigations I’m executing now:
1) Temporarily increase the concurrency window for Borealis pool by +15% (will add burst capacity and is safe for 10–20m).
2) Add a short-term backpressure rule at the edge to convert aggressive client retries into 429 throttles with a capped retry-after to prevent amplification.
3) Disable one non-critical async prefetch job that is consuming kernel slots in the pool.

Pushing changes now — ETA for first measurable effect: 10–15 minutes after change. Attaching our mitigation checklist that I’ll update as we go.

Attachment: redwood-mitigation-checklist.pdf

— Marissa
Senior Infra SW Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Jensen <tom.jensen@borealis.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] Traffic spike -> 5xx/429s + client retry amplification

Additional diagnostics:
- Root-pattern: client SDK aggressive retry loop -> bursts of short-lived connections -> ingress rate-limiter trips -> 429s -> clients immediately retry -> overload. Not seeing model-level OOMs currently (no GPU OOM traces), but runtime thread pool saturation is visible.
- Correlated a recent SDK rollout (v3.6.2) from the customer side that introduced zero-backoff retries for certain error classes.

Temporary tactical steps I recommend now (applied in this order):
A) Edge-level token bucket to smooth spikes (implemented; smoothing should take effect within ~5m).
B) Shorten KV cache TTL flush window for the affected model instance to avoid repeated cold-cache misses while we scale.
C) If traffic still remains high after smoothing, route a percentage of traffic to a warm-compatible model variant (fallback) to reduce per-request overhead.

ETA: Expect visible improvement 10–25 minutes after edge smoothing; full normalization 30–45 minutes assuming we can sustain the +15% burst.

— Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Borealis service status — interim update (ETA ~30–45m)

Tom — quick customer-facing update that you can share with your teams: 

Status: We are seeing elevated 5xx/429 errors caused by retry amplification from a customer SDK rollout combined with ingress rate limiting. Our team has taken immediate steps to stabilize traffic:
- Increased dedicated pool burst capacity (+15%) and removed a non-critical prefetch job.
- Implemented edge smoothing (token-bucket) to blunt retry spikes.
- Shortened KV cache TTLs and prepared an A/B fallback route to a compatible warm model if needed.

Expected impact: symptomatic improvement within 10–25 minutes; full normalization ~30–45 minutes from now. We will post the same update to https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-20270711-072 in the next 10 minutes.

Next steps:
- I’ll send another update when the error rate is back to baseline or if we need an expanded workaround.
- If you’d like a written postmortem and a schedule for a follow-up runbook review with your SRE/engineering leads, we can arrange that this week.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re treating this as P0 and will keep you updated.

Soojin Lee
